newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking trims leading Hungarian stocks.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking trims leading Hungarian stocks.

text.p: Leading heavy-weight Hungarian stocks drifted lower on Thursday as investors decided to lock in profits after early gains, likely bringing the BUX index down from Wednesday's record level, traders said.
"I think investors are cashing profits in," one trader said.
On Wednesday the BUX index closed at a third successive record high of 5,815.38 points.
The losers included pharmaceuticals Richter, oil company MOL and chemicals TVK.

Richter, which on Wednesday benefited from news that Germany's Linde won a 100 million German mark contract to build a plant for Richter, continued to rise to a new record high of 11,980 forints. But it later eased and at 1156 GMT traded at 11,650 forints.
MOL, after rising to 3,750 forints, plummeted around two percent and at 1141 GMT it traded at 3,520.
TVK firmed to a daily high of 2,630 forints but retreated to 2,525 by 1153 GMT.
